page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.18xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine features 72 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 vCPUs running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, along with 288.0 GB of system memory. This hardware allocation establishes a standardized memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, aligning with general-purpose enterprise computing parameters.

Network infrastructure for this instance provides a baseline bandwidth of 33 Gbps, supporting stable throughput for data transfer and cloud storage operations. The server does not contain local NVMe SSD storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Consequently, disk persistent storage depends entirely on network-attached block storage devices, and graphics acceleration is unavailable.

The high physical core count and total memory footprint offer strong compute density for consolidation of enterprise application tiers. Cost efficiency is driven by high resource allocation on a single host, minimizing instance fragmentation. Suitable workload fits include web app hosting, backend microservices, continuous integration pipelines, software compilation tasks, and relational databases using attached block volumes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.18xlarge is a general-purpose instance driven by 72 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 vCPUs clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 288.0 GB of memory on an x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. The system exhibits a standardized 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, offering 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU for uniform processing efficiency across multi-threaded applications. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 33 Gbps, facilitating high throughput for server-to-server communication and cloud storage traffic. The instance includes no local SSD storage and no integrated GPU accelerators, requiring reliance on remote block storage solutions for persistent data workloads. With high hardware density and stable network capacity, this server type provides balanced resource allocation without specialized hardware overhead. It is designed to support scalable enterprise web serving, microservice deployments, software compilation, CI/CD execution, and general database management.
